name: Lo & Sons
description: US direct-to-consumer bag brand founded by the Lo family, known for travel-light weekender bags, backpacks and work-to-gym bags that combine function and style. It recruits loyal customers, micro-influencers and large publishers into an affiliate program run through the Impact network.

evidence.summary: Lo & Sons' own Affiliates page (fetched) invites loyal customers, micro-influencers and large-scale publishers to apply. Getting started: join through the Impact.com network (free), get approved, then search for Lo & Sons inside Impact to access text links and banners and earn commission on every referred bag purchase. Program questions go to partnerships@loandsons.com, published on the page. The brand's own page publishes no commission rate and no earnings-cap statement, so commission_cap is unknown.

Shopper.com's partnership listing (fetched) reports a 5% payout per sale for the Lo & Sons program, while affiliatesaz.com's directory describes the Lo & Sons commission as 'varies by product'. Because the two fetched sources conflict and the brand itself publishes no rate, commission_rate is recorded as null with the conflict documented here. No fetched source states any earnings cap or creator count, so commission_cap and creator_saturation are unknown.

reasons: Travel-light bags are a core, high-intent niche for travel and everyday-carry creators.
The brand explicitly welcomes micro-influencers alongside large publishers, widening access for smaller creators.
A published partnerships email and a clear Impact application path make the program easy to reach and verify.
Commission rate is not published by the brand and directory reports conflict (5% vs varies by product), which caps the compensation score.

name: Solgaard
description: Sustainable travel gear brand founded in 2016, known for suitcases, backpacks, watches and speakers made with ocean-bound plastic through its Solgaard x ShoreTide material program. It runs an affiliate program with a dedicated affiliate team, recruited by email application and paid monthly via FlexOffers.

evidence.summary: Solgaard's own affiliate page (fetched) targets 'global citizens passionate about travel' and offers 'a great commission structure, a dedicated affiliate team, regular deals and an easy-to-use affiliate platform'. Joining is by email application to solgaard@dmipartners.com with URLs, handles, audience stats and brand alignment. The page publishes no rate and no earnings-cap statement, so commission_cap is unknown.

GetLasso's program listing (fetched) reports 10% per sale with a 90-day cookie for Solgaard; LinkWhisper and AffiliateCollective independently report the same 10% rate and 90-day cookie, and a MaxFunnels review reports monthly payment via FlexOffers. The 10% rate is corroborated across three fetched sources, so it is recorded. No fetched source states an earnings cap or an absolute creator count, so commission_cap and creator_saturation are unknown.

reasons: Sustainable luggage and backpacks sit squarely in the travel-gear niche, with a strong story angle around ocean plastic.
A corroborated 10% commission with a long 90-day cookie is above average for travel gear.
Application is a direct email to a named affiliate team, and the brand promises dedicated affiliate support.
No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap stays honestly unknown.

name: July
description: Melbourne-founded direct-to-consumer luggage brand known for design-led polycarbonate suitcases, bags and personalisation, selling in Australia, New Zealand and the United States. July runs a 'content partner' affiliate program promoted from its own site footer.

evidence.summary: July's own site (fetched) runs a 'Brand Affiliates' page: 'Partner with us. Love July? Apply to become a content partner and earn commission on sales.' The live page does not publish a rate or any earnings-cap statement, so commission_cap is unknown.

Published rates conflict across fetched sources: a mirrored copy of July's affiliate page reports 8% on all luggage and accessories, rising to 9% on sales over $500 and 10% over $1,000 with a 45-day referral cookie, while older network directories report 4% (AffJumbo, 30-day cookie, 60-day hold) and 6% (Mopubi). Because the sources conflict, commission_rate is recorded as null with the conflict documented here. No fetched source states an earnings cap or creator count.

reasons: Design-led luggage is a proven, high-intent category for travel creators, and July is a recognised DTC brand in AU/NZ/US.
July recruits content partners directly from its own site, signalling an active creator channel.
Reported tiered rates up to 10% are attractive, but published figures conflict (4%, 6%, 8% tiered), so the rate is recorded as null and compensation is scored cautiously.
No earnings-cap statement is published anywhere fetched, so the cap stays unknown.

name: Pact

evidence.summary: BravoDM's checked program facts (fetched; program checked October 2026) describe Pact's affiliate program as a flat 8% commission, plus a separate Influencer Program the brand recruits for by invitation. AffJumbo's listing independently reports the same flat 8% with a 30-day cookie and a $100 payout threshold, so the 8% rate is recorded. No fetched source states an earnings cap, so commission_cap is unknown.

Pact's own influencer signup page (fetched via the brand's site) states the brand is 'currently revamping our influencer program' and cannot accept new influencer applications at this time, with a relaunch planned within weeks. The affiliate route remains the open path; the influencer pause lowers the availability score. FlexOffers also lists a Pact Apparel affiliate program page. No creator count is published, so creator_saturation is unknown.

reasons: Organic everyday basics and maternity are a steady, content-friendly fashion niche with a clear sustainability angle.
A flat 8% commission is corroborated by two independent fetched sources, including one checked in October 2026.
The separate influencer program is invite-based and currently paused for a revamp, which limits creator access today.
No earnings-cap statement is published, so the cap stays unknown.
